# Installation {#sec-installation}

## Review workstation

The supported no-code Windows lifecycle is `FIRST_RUN.bat` ->
`START_DR_SCREENING.bat` -> browser. No machine-wide Administrator access is
required. The release includes a prebuilt frontend, so normal workstation use
does not require Node.js or npm.

```{=latex}
\Needspace{18\baselineskip}
```

**Steps (Windows).**

```text
git clone https://github.com/siriponsri/dr-support-screening-poc.git
cd dr-support-screening-poc
FIRST_RUN.bat
START_DR_SCREENING.bat
```

**Expected result.** The workstation serves `http://127.0.0.1:8000/app/` and
opens it in the default browser. Daily `START_DR_SCREENING.bat` calls reuse the
project environment and prebuilt frontend; they never run npm. Use
`STOP_DR_SCREENING.bat` to stop only the repository-managed process.

Use `CHECK_SYSTEM.bat` for a read-only installation diagnostic. Developer
checkouts install test, DICOM, and browser-test extras with `uv sync` as
described in the developer guide.

## Linux server checkout

Place the release at `/opt/dr-support-screening-poc` when using the included systemd unit. Keep runtime assets in `local-state/` or another private path. Never commit model weights, review databases, or secret environment files.

## Configuration

Use `.env.example` only as a reference. Supply tokens through the private process environment or an approved secret manager. The model-server example is `deployment/model-server.env.example`; `docs/operations/CONFIGURATION.md` lists every variable and its safe default.
